Fact.Name: Form 2106 employee name
Fact.Description: The employee name printed in the Form 2106 header. This is a form-specific transcription field; it does not replace the return's filer identity.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 occupation
Fact.Description: The occupation in which the employee incurred the reported business expenses, printed in the Form 2106 header.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 employee SSN first segment
Fact.Description: The three-digit area segment of the employee's Social Security number printed in the Form 2106 header.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 employee SSN second segment
Fact.Description: The two-digit group segment of the employee's Social Security number printed in the Form 2106 header.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 employee SSN third segment
Fact.Description: The four-digit serial segment of the employee's Social Security number printed in the Form 2106 header.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 filer meets a listed employee-expense category
Fact.Description: Attest that the filer is an Armed Forces reservist, qualified performing artist, fee-basis state or local official, or employee with impairment-related work expenses.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 1 vehicle expense
Fact.Description: Vehicle expense transferred from Form 2106 Part II line 22 or line 29.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 2 parking, tolls, and local transportation
Fact.Description: Parking, tolls, and non-commuting transportation expenses not involving overnight travel.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 3 overnight travel expense
Fact.Description: Travel while away from home overnight, excluding meals.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 4 other non-meal business expenses
Fact.Description: Employee business expenses not included on lines 1 through 3, excluding meals.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 5 meals expense
Fact.Description: Meal expenses before reimbursement and deductibility limitations.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 6 column A total expenses
Fact.Description: Sum of lines 1 through 4, other than meals.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 6 column B total meals expenses
Fact.Description: Column B carries the line 5 meal-expense amount.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 7 column A reimbursements
Fact.Description: Employer reimbursements for column A expenses, including Form W-2 box 12 code L, excluding amounts already reported in box 1.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 7 column B reimbursements
Fact.Description: Employer reimbursements attributable to the meal expenses in column B.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 8 column A after reimbursements
Fact.Description: Column A line 6 less column A line 7, floored at zero.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 8 column B after reimbursements
Fact.Description: Column B line 6 less column B line 7, floored at zero; this is the pre-limit meal expense amount.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 column A reimbursement excess reported as income
Fact.Description: Column A line 7 reimbursements above line 6 expenses, reported on Form 1040 line 1a. Exported for the income-module successor.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 9 column A deduction
Fact.Description: Column A line 9 carries the amount from line 8.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 meals subject to Department of Transportation hours-of-service limits
Fact.Description: Answer true when the employee's meals were incurred while away from home during or incident to a period of duty subject to the Department of Transportation hours-of-service limits. This selects the statutory 80% meal deduction instead of the general 50% limitation. Answer false for the general rule; an unanswered answer uses the conservative 50% rule.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 9 column B deductible meals
Fact.Description: Form 2106 line 9 column B is the line 8 column B meal expense after the printed limitation: 50% generally, or 80% when the employee answers the Department of Transportation hours-of-service question true. The complete-safe unanswered Boolean takes the general 50% branch.

Fact.Name: Form 2106 line 10 total employee business expense deduction
Fact.Description: Sum of both line 9 columns. Exported as the Schedule 1 line 12 successor input.

Fact.Name: Return files Form 2106
Fact.Description:
True when the filer attests eligibility and the modeled line 10 deduction or line-1a reimbursement excess is positive. Vehicle substantiation-only filings are outside this gate.
A PRINT GATE OWES A DECIDED ANSWER, and the first case is that and nothing more. The eligibility attestation is the first question Who Must File asks, and a Switch with no catch-all runs off its end when every When is Incomplete, so on a return that never answers /writableForm2106QualifyingFiler this fact used to resolve Incomplete: the renderer was handed neither a yes nor a no about a printed form. The first case answers the decided no that an unselected Form 2106 deserves. It is the same guarded-presence shape /form8582ReturnFilesThisForm uses, and it moves nothing on a return that answers the attestation, because the later two cases already partition that population. Pinned by form2106-key-absent and form2106-empty-unrelated-collection, both of which were measured Incomplete before the edit and Complete false after, against form2106-explicit-not-qualifying and form2106-answered-zero, which were already false.
WHAT IS STILL UNDECIDED, stated rather than left to be found: a filer who attests eligibility but has not answered the Part I expense boxes reaches the second case, whose Then is Incomplete because line 10 is. That is a real remaining gap in the gate, not a value the dictionary may invent - deciding it means choosing between suppressing a form the filer may owe and attaching one with blank money lines. form2106-eligible-unanswered-details pins it as it stands.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Form 2106 eligibility attested but Part I not answered
Fact.Description:
Refuses a return on which the filer attests being an Armed Forces reservist, a qualified performing artist, a fee-basis state or local government official, or an employee with impairment-related work expenses (/writableForm2106QualifyingFiler answered true) while the Part I expense and reimbursement boxes line 10 and the reimbursement excess are figured from remain unanswered. On that return /form2106ReturnFilesThisForm can say neither yes nor no: a no would drop a form the filer attested to owing, and a yes would attach a Form 2106 whose money lines are blank. The fact is TRUE exactly when that print gate is not complete, so it fires on no other return: an unanswered attestation, a no, and every answered Part I leave the gate decided and this fact false.
SCREEN: "You told us you are filing Form 2106 as a reservist, performing artist, fee-basis official, or employee with impairment-related work expenses, but the Form 2106 expense and reimbursement amounts are not entered. Enter them (enter 0 where you have none) so the form can be completed, or change your answer to the Form 2106 question."
